introduction: A carry_patch workspace keeps an ordered list of patch branches and an integration branch rebuilt from the upstream head plus those patches. This package manages the list, extends the sync to fetch upstream and reconcile the patches, runs the rebuild job, and serves the rebuild, rerere and patch-status routes.

glossary.branch resolution: How an added patch's branch is found: in the workspace's own repository, in the fork's already-fetched copy, or by fetching the fork; reported as local, origin_tracking, origin_fetch or skipped.
glossary.divergence policy: What a sync does when the workspace's copy of a patch branch and the fork's have diverged: replace the workspace's with the fork's tip, keeping the old one, or report the divergence and leave it alone.
glossary.integration branch: The branch a carry_patch workspace rebuilds from the upstream head plus its active patches. It is never pushed by the branch push route and is never a registered patch.
glossary.merged upstream: A patch whose changes the upstream has taken, found by ancestry, by content, or by a pull request number in a recent upstream commit message, according to the squash_merge_detection setting.
glossary.patch: A branch registered in a carry_patch workspace's ordered list, applied onto the upstream base by a rebuild. It has a position, a status and, where the fork is its source, a record of how it stood against the fork at the last sync.
glossary.rebuild: The job that recreates the integration branch from the upstream head and the patches, in position order, by the chosen strategy.
glossary.stale snapshot: A patch tip or upstream head that moved while a rebuild was applying patches. The running job keeps the tips it started with and one follow-up rebuild is queued afterwards.

requirements.title: Adding patches to the list
requirements.rationale: The add is the only route that touches the repository to create a branch, and its batch semantics are the most exacting part of the patch endpoints.

criteria.condition: a single patch is added to a carry_patch workspace with a branch that can be resolved
criteria.action: add it to the list with status active and report how its branch was resolved
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 with the patch carrying status "active", its position, and a branch resolution of local, origin_tracking, origin_fetch or skipped

criteria.action: insert a patch at the position given, moving the patches at and after it down by one, and append when the position is past the end or omitted
criteria.contract: after the add the positions are 1 to n with no gap and no repeat, and the new patch sits where it was asked to

criteria.action: resolve an added patch's branch by trying the workspace's own repository, then the fork's already-fetched copy, then — only with patch_branch_source origin — a fetch from the fork, stopping at the first that succeeds
criteria.contract: the reported resolution names which succeeded; a branch found locally writes nothing; one found as the fork's copy or fetched is created in the repository; with skip_branch_check none of this happens and the resolution is skipped

criteria.condition: an add names a branch already in the list
criteria.action: answer with the existing patch instead of refusing
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the existing patch unchanged; without if_not_exists the same request is HTTP 409

criteria.condition: several patches are added in one request
criteria.action: check every element's syntax first in array order, then every element's branch, and add all of them or none
criteria.contract: a batch whose first element names a missing branch and whose second has an invalid position answers for the second element's syntax; a branch failure refuses the whole batch and adds no patch, while branches created for earlier elements remain and resolve as local next time

criteria.condition: an add has a missing or empty branch name, names the integration branch, gives a position below 1, targets a standard or archived workspace, or names a branch that cannot be resolved
criteria.action: refuse the request and add nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 in the error envelope; in a batch the message begins "patch[i]: " naming the element; the list is unchanged

criteria.condition: an add names a branch already in the list without if_not_exists, names one branch twice in a batch, needs the repository while the lock is held, or cannot fetch from the fork
criteria.action: refuse the request and add nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 for a duplicate and for a branch repeated within a batch, HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_busy for a held lock, HTTP 502 with error_type origin_fetch_failed for a failed fork fetch; the list is unchanged

requirements.title: Reading and changing patches
requirements.rationale: Position and status drive what a rebuild applies, so a list that is not contiguous or a status that can be set to deleted breaks the rebuild rather than the route.

criteria.condition: a workspace's patches are listed
criteria.action: return them in position order, leaving deleted ones out
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with an array in ascending position order and no patch of status deleted; a standard workspace answers an empty array

criteria.condition: one patch is read
criteria.action: return it, a deleted one included, with the SHA of a replaced tip where one is kept
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the patch; replaced_sha is the 40-character SHA when a backup exists and is absent when there is none, when the workspace has no repository, or when the lookup fails, which never fails the request

criteria.condition: a patch is updated with a position, status, description or upstream pull request
criteria.action: change only those fields and keep the positions contiguous
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the updated patch; a branch_name in the body is ignored; after a position change the positions are 1 to n with no gap

criteria.condition: an update gives an invalid status or the status deleted, gives a position outside 1 to n, names a patch that does not exist, or targets a deleted patch
criteria.action: refuse the request and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 for an invalid status or position, HTTP 404 for a patch not found, HTTP 409 for a deleted patch; the patch is unchanged

criteria.action: keep the positions of a workspace's patches contiguous from 1 after every add, update, removal, restore, reorder and rebuild
criteria.contract: for any sequence of those operations the positions of the non-deleted patches are exactly 1 to n in order

requirements.title: Removing, restoring and reordering
requirements.rationale: A patch removed by mistake must be recoverable, and a reorder that silently drops a patch changes what ships.

criteria.condition: a patch is removed
criteria.action: take it out of the list, close the positions and discard any backup of a replaced tip
criteria.contract: HTTP 204; the remaining patches hold positions 1 to n-1; discarding the backup is best effort and never changes the answer

criteria.condition: a deleted patch is restored
criteria.action: return it to the list as active at the end, clearing the time it was deleted
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the patch at status active, at the last position, and deleted_at null

criteria.condition: the whole list is reordered with a list of patch ids
criteria.action: set the positions to the order given
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with every patch in the new order; the first id holds position 1 and so on

criteria.condition: a reorder does not name every patch of the workspace exactly once, or a restore names a patch that is not deleted, a standard workspace or an archived one
criteria.action: refuse the request and change no position or status
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 for a reorder that is empty while patches exist, omits an id, repeats one or names another workspace's patch, and for a restore of a patch that is not deleted; HTTP 404 for a patch not found; the list is unchanged

requirements.title: Resetting a patch branch to the fork
requirements.rationale: It is the escape hatch when the workspace's copy and the fork's have diverged, and it is the operation that can discard commits.

criteria.action: check, in order, that the workspace is not archived and is carry_patch, that its status is ready, that the patch exists, that its branch is not the integration branch, and that its status is active, conflict or disabled
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 for an archived or standard workspace and for the integration branch, HTTP 409 for a workspace that is not ready and for a merged_upstream or deleted patch, HTTP 404 for a patch that does not exist, each given by the first failing check

criteria.action: move the branch by the first rule that applies: create it at the fork's tip when the workspace lacks it, write nothing when the commits match, fast-forward when the fork's tip descends from the workspace's, and otherwise replace it
criteria.contract: the reported action is created, none, fast_forwarded or replaced accordingly, and the branch afterwards is at the fork's tip in every case but none

criteria.condition: a reset moves a patch branch
criteria.guard: the move discards commits the workspace held
criteria.action: keep the old tip where a replaced tip is kept for this deployment, replacing any earlier backup
criteria.contract: the old tip is recoverable afterwards and is reported as replaced_sha; an earlier backup for the same branch is superseded

criteria.condition: a reset moves a patch branch
criteria.guard: the patch is active or conflict and auto_rebuild_after_sync is not false
criteria.action: queue a rebuild and report it
criteria.contract: the answer carries rebuild_triggered true and the queued job's id; a disabled patch queues none; an already queued or running rebuild is not duplicated and rebuild_triggered is false

criteria.condition: the fork has no such branch, another operation changed the branch while the reset ran, the fork could not be fetched, the lock is held, or the branch moved but the patch could not be read back
criteria.action: refuse or report the failure without leaving the patch record inconsistent
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error_type missing_on_origin, ref_changed or workspace_busy as applicable, HTTP 502 with error_type origin_fetch_failed or naming a credential failure, HTTP 500 when the branch moved and could not be read back

requirements.title: Syncing a carry-patch workspace
requirements.rationale: Eight ordered steps whose partial failure still has effects; written as a single success or failure it loses work the caller is owed.

criteria.action: fetch the upstream rather than the fork, fetching the fork as well only when patch_branch_source is origin
criteria.contract: with patch_branch_source hub no request reaches the fork and origin_fetched is false; with origin the fork is fetched, pruning branches it deleted, and origin_fetched is true

criteria.action: perform the sync's steps in the documented order: resolve the fork's credentials, fetch upstream, fetch the fork, detect a force-push, refresh the patch branches, detect patches merged upstream, write the sync fields, and queue a rebuild
criteria.contract: an earlier step's failure prevents the later steps; the effects of the steps already completed are those the reference states for that failure

criteria.condition: the upstream advanced and the previous upstream head is not an ancestor of the new one
criteria.action: report that the upstream history was rewritten without treating it as an error
criteria.contract: force_push_detected is true and the sync still answers 200; the rebuild applies the patches to the rewritten upstream

criteria.condition: a sync refreshes the patch branches
criteria.action: bring each active, conflict or disabled patch's branch to the fork's tip by the first rule that applies, and record how each stood
criteria.contract: each branch is reported as missing_on_origin, created, none, fast_forwarded, replaced or diverged; under the replace policy a diverged branch is replaced with the old tip kept and patches_diverged is empty, and under the report policy it is left alone and listed in patches_diverged; the integration branch is never refreshed; each patch's origin state, SHA and time are recorded, and with patch_branch_source hub those three are cleared

criteria.condition: the upstream advanced, or a branch of an active or conflict patch moved
criteria.guard: the squash_merge_detection setting permits the strategy
criteria.action: mark as merged upstream the patches the upstream has taken, by ancestry, by content, or by a pull request number in a recent upstream commit message
criteria.contract: ancestry_only uses ancestry alone, content_based uses content and the pull request number, and both uses all three; a matched patch's status becomes merged_upstream, its origin fields are cleared, and its branch is listed in patches_merged

criteria.condition: the upstream advanced, a branch of an active or conflict patch moved, or a patch became merged upstream
criteria.guard: auto_rebuild_after_sync is not false and no rebuild is queued or running
criteria.action: queue one rebuild and report it
criteria.contract: rebuild_triggered is true and rebuild_job_id carries the job's id; with auto_rebuild_after_sync false, or with a rebuild already queued or running, rebuild_triggered is false and rebuild_job_id is absent rather than null

criteria.condition: refreshing a patch branch fails
criteria.action: end the sync in failure while keeping the outcomes already reached and the rebuild already owed
criteria.contract: HTTP 500 whose message distinguishes a failed branch write, a failed ancestry comparison and a failed working-state update; the outcomes already reached are recorded; a rebuild is queued for branches already moved unless auto_rebuild_after_sync is false; neither upstream_head_sha nor last_sync_at is written

criteria.condition: a carry-patch sync completes
criteria.action: answer with the workspace and the sync's own fields
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with every workspace field plus patches_merged, rebuild_triggered, force_push_detected, origin_fetched, and, with patch_branch_source origin, patches_synced and patches_diverged; sync_error is not used on this path and last_sync_at is updated by every completed sync whether or not anything advanced

requirements.title: How a rebuild runs
requirements.rationale: This is the operation the whole feature exists for, and the one whose lock discipline lets other work proceed while it runs.

criteria.condition: a rebuild runs
criteria.action: start from the upstream head it fetches at its start and apply the patches in position order
criteria.contract: the job records the upstream head it started from; the patches are attempted in ascending position order and the result lists them in that order

criteria.action: skip a patch that is merged upstream, disabled or deleted, or whose branch does not exist, recording why
criteria.contract: each skipped patch is reported with status skipped and a reason of merged_upstream, disabled, deleted or branch_not_found, and contributes nothing to the result

criteria.condition: applying a patch conflicts after a recorded resolution has been replayed
criteria.guard: the job's fail mode is fail_fast
criteria.action: end the job as failed
criteria.contract: the job's status is failed with the conflicting patch and its files reported; with fail_mode continue the patch is marked conflict, its changes are left out and the later patches are still attempted

criteria.condition: a rebuild reaches its end
criteria.action: set the integration branch to the result, mark patches merged upstream as deleted and close the positions
criteria.contract: the integration branch is at the rebuilt head; each merged_upstream patch has status deleted with deleted_at set; the remaining positions are 1 to n; the job reports the new and the previous integration head

criteria.condition: a rebuild completes
criteria.action: force-push the integration branch to the fork without letting a failure fail the job
criteria.contract: the job reports integration_branch_pushed true on success; on failure the job still completes and the field reflects that the push did not happen

criteria.condition: a rebuild completes
criteria.guard: a patch tip or the upstream head moved while it was applying patches
criteria.action: keep the result built from the tips it started with and queue one follow-up rebuild
criteria.contract: the completed job's result reflects the tips it started with; exactly one follow-up rebuild is queued, submitted by the system rather than a user

criteria.action: hold the workspace lock only while fetching the upstream at the start and while updating the integration branch at the end
criteria.contract: a sync, a merge, a rerere forget, a rollback and a branch push all succeed while a rebuild is applying patches; archive and reclone answer 409 workspace_busy for the whole rebuild

criteria.action: make each patch's result readable as soon as that patch finishes
criteria.contract: reading a running job returns the results of the patches completed so far, growing as the job proceeds

requirements.title: The rebuild routes
requirements.rationale: A queued job is only useful if a client can follow it, stop it and undo it.

criteria.condition: a rebuild is submitted for a carry_patch workspace that is ready, has at least one active or conflict patch and has no rebuild queued or running
criteria.action: queue the job, taking the strategy and fail mode from the body or the workspace's settings
criteria.contract: HTTP 202 with the queued job carrying its id, type, status queued and payload; a body naming strategy or fail_mode overrides the setting and an absent body uses the settings

criteria.condition: a rebuild is submitted for a workspace that is not carry_patch or not ready, with no active or conflict patch, with an invalid strategy or fail mode, or while one is queued or running
criteria.action: refuse the request and queue nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with error_type workspace_mode_mismatch, no_active_patches, or no type for a workspace that is not ready or an invalid field; HTTP 409 with error_type concurrent_rebuild for one already queued or running

criteria.condition: a workspace's rebuilds are listed or one is read
criteria.action: return the jobs newest first, or the one named with its per-patch results
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the jobs or the job; a job of another workspace or an unknown id is HTTP 404

criteria.condition: a queued rebuild is cancelled, or a dead-lettered one is requeued
criteria.action: change its state accordingly
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with status cancelled for a cancel, and the job back at queued for a requeue; a job that is not queued is HTTP 409 on cancel, and one that is not dead-lettered, or whose workspace already has a rebuild queued or running, is HTTP 409 on requeue

criteria.condition: a completed rebuild is rolled back
criteria.action: set the integration branch back to the head it had before that rebuild
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 reporting the SHA rolled back to, and the integration branch is at it; a job with no previous head is HTTP 409, a held lock is HTTP 409 workspace_busy, and a failure to reset the branch is HTTP 500

criteria.condition: the rebuild preview is requested
criteria.action: predict for each patch that is not disabled or merged upstream whether it would apply, without writing anything
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with a result per patch of would_succeed with a resulting tree, or would_conflict with the conflicting files; a predicted conflict does not stop the later predictions; a patch whose branch does not exist is reported would_succeed; no ref or object of the repository changes; a workspace that is not carry_patch is HTTP 400

requirements.title: The rerere routes
requirements.rationale: A recorded resolution that cannot be inspected or dropped is one a person cannot correct when it is wrong.

criteria.condition: a workspace's recorded resolutions are listed
criteria.action: return them newest first with their identity, path, recorded time and whether a resolution will be replayed
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with a resolutions array, empty when there are none; path is null for a resolution recorded by an earlier rebuild; resolved is true only when a resolution will be replayed

criteria.condition: a resolution is forgotten by its identity, or by a path that is currently in conflict
criteria.action: remove it so the conflict is reported again
criteria.contract: HTTP 204; the entry is gone from the listing and the next occurrence of that conflict is reported rather than replayed

criteria.condition: a forget is called with an empty or invalid pathspec, names no recorded entry, or finds the workspace's lock held
criteria.action: refuse the request and remove nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 for an empty or invalid pathspec, checked before the workspace is looked up; HTTP 404 when no entry matches the identity or no resolution is recorded for the path; HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_busy for a held lock

requirements.title: The patch-status dashboard
requirements.rationale: One answer a person reads to know whether the stack is healthy, which means its counts have to agree with the list they summarise.

criteria.condition: the patch-status dashboard is requested for a carry_patch workspace
criteria.action: return the workspace's state, its latest rebuild, every non-deleted patch with its latest rebuild result, and the summary counts
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the documented object; patches are in position order; each patch carries its latest rebuild result or null, and its conflicting files only where that result is a conflict; last_rebuild is the latest job's id and status, or null

criteria.action: make the summary counts agree with the patches the same answer lists
criteria.contract: total_patches equals the length of the patches array and equals active plus merged_upstream plus conflict plus disabled; patches_diverged and patches_missing_on_origin count the patches whose origin state says so and are 0 with patch_branch_source hub; total_rerere_resolutions is 0 when the resolutions cannot be read

criteria.condition: the dashboard is requested for a workspace that is not carry_patch
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 in the error envelope

requirements.title: Triggering a rebuild from a push
requirements.rationale: This is what makes the stack rebuild itself when an agent pushes, and duplicating the trigger would queue a rebuild per push.

criteria.condition: a push to the git server accepts an update of a registered patch branch on a carry_patch workspace
criteria.guard: the auto_rebuild_after_push setting is not false
criteria.action: queue a rebuild without making the push wait for it
criteria.contract: the push's answer does not wait for the rebuild; a rebuild is queued for that workspace; with auto_rebuild_after_push false none is queued

criteria.action: queue at most one rebuild for a workspace at a time, whatever triggered it
criteria.contract: when a rebuild is already queued or running, a push, a sync or a reset queues no second one and reports that none was triggered

execution_paths.title: A patch is registered and the stack rebuilt

steps.action: adds a branch as a patch to a carry_patch workspace
resolves the branch in the workspace's repository, appends the patch as active and reports the resolution
submits a rebuild and receives the queued job
takes the workspace lock, fetches the upstream head and releases the lock
applies each active patch onto the upstream head in position order
retakes the lock, sets the integration branch, closes the positions and completes the job
polls the job and reads a result for every patch

execution_paths.title: An upstream advance is absorbed by a sync and a rebuild

steps.action: syncs a carry_patch workspace whose upstream has advanced
fetches the upstream, detects one patch as merged upstream and writes the sync fields
queues a rebuild and answers with its id and the merged patch's branch
applies the remaining patches onto the new upstream head
marks the merged patch deleted, closes the positions and sets the integration branch
reads the patch-status dashboard and sees the new integration head and each patch's result

execution_paths.title: A conflict is recorded once and replayed on the next rebuild

steps.action: submits a rebuild with the continue fail mode on a stack whose second patch conflicts
reports the conflict and its files for that patch
marks the patch conflict, leaves its changes out, applies the later patches and completes the job
resolves the conflict so the resolution is recorded
submits another rebuild of the same stack
replays the recorded resolution and applies the patch cleanly

execution_paths.title: A diverged patch branch is reported and then reset

steps.action: syncs a workspace whose patch branches come from the fork under the report policy
fetches the fork, finds one patch branch diverged and lists it in patches_diverged
calls reset-to-origin for that patch
moves the branch to the fork's tip, keeps the old tip where replaced tips are kept and queues a rebuild
reads the patch and finds the replaced SHA and the queued rebuild's id
